selected.label: UX-VERIFY: verification and claims
selected.question: What must an agent run on an interface change, and what may it claim afterwards about accessibility, performance and usability?

selected.label: UX-A11Y: accessibility authoring
selected.question: Which accessibility properties must an agent build into interface code and page templates by default, and which ARIA and custom widgets must it refuse to write?

selected.label: UX-STATE: interface states
selected.question: Which states must every view, async action and form render, with which indicator at which wait, and how does a rule detect a missing state?

selected.label: UX-TEXT: interface text
selected.question: What must runtime interface text contain, and which words and string constructions must an agent never ship?

selected.label: UX-CLI: CLI interaction
selected.question: Above the pinned stream, colour, prompt and exit contracts, what does a CLI owe a first-time human and an everyday user?

selected.label: UX-ACT: consequential actions
selected.question: When does an action need confirmation, undo, a dry run, typed confirmation, human approval or nothing, whether it is clicked, typed or called by an agent?

selected.label: UX-AI: AI features
selected.question: What must a human-facing LLM interface disclose, show and refuse to render, and which of those duties are now law?

selected.label: UX-AGENT: agent-facing interfaces
selected.question: When the caller is an agent, what must a tool, CLI or MCP server provide?

frameCorrections: 1. grim-gui is a skeleton (74 lines, 0 interactive elements), not a GUI to govern (product-audit/ui-code-posture.md, product-audit/distribution-posture.md).

2. The VS Code extension is the fleet's real GUI (42 production files, 24,957 lines, 183 message calls, 0 withProgress) and the audits did not measure it; this adds the editor-extension-surfaces dive (product-audit/config-inventory.md, map measurements).

3. The shared @ocx-sh/theme (139 files, 5+ consuming sites) is the main web target, and the frame omitted the catalog and indexer renderers (product-audit/ui-code-posture.md, product-audit/site-shape.md).
4. Existing UX configuration lives outside the catalog: six ocx-theme-* skills (157,752 B) and the extension CLAUDE.md (product-audit/config-inventory.md).
5. An accessibility gate already exists (Lighthouse 100 on ocx.sh PRs, axe in 47 deep-tier specs); the gaps are Grimoire docs, GUIs and a score-only gate (product-audit/ui-code-posture.md).
6. The CLI and GUI split falsifier fires: CLI duties need their own reference skill on a different trigger (product-frame.md falsifiers, product-audit/cli-first-run.md).
7. The CLI is the primary surface; its uncovered ground is help structure, --version, typo recovery, first run, error anatomy and JSON reliability (product-audit/cli-first-run.md).
8. Rules need Detect and Severity, in the Spectrum agent audit format (product-audit/exemplar-design-systems.md).

9. The checkable gaps are text, motion and target size: theme tokens below 24 px, 0 reduced-motion blocks in Grimoire docs (product-audit/exemplar-design-systems.md, product-audit/ui-code-posture.md).
10. There is no design system to copy wholesale: Polaris archived, Material in maintenance, shadcn lacks a11y automation (product-audit/exemplar-design-systems.md).
11. Vendor agent configs (Spectrum audit, USWDS skill) are routed to, not restated (product-audit/exemplar-design-systems.md).
12. 'Never remove the outline' is a false rule here: 15 of 16 outline:none sites carry a replacement; Detect must check for it (product-audit/ui-code-posture.md).
13. UX guidance decays like platform facts; every reference file carries a dated-facts table (ux-topic-map/accessibility.md row 32, ux-topic-map/recent-shifts.md row 27).
14. The fleet has no analytics or field data by decision; no rule may depend on field metrics (product-audit/distribution-posture.md).
15. There are no commerce flows in the fleet; deceptive-pattern and cancellation material is deferred, not dropped (product-audit/distribution-posture.md, product-audit/messaging-inventory.md).
16. css-theming already loads on 24 globs; ux-quality must not restate tokens and must stay small (product-audit/config-inventory.md).
17. Rule-ownership collisions are a known failure (DOC-PLAIN-15 precedent); UX-TEXT must resolve DOC-PLAIN-01 explicitly (product-audit/config-inventory.md).
18. The MkDocs sites run vendor UI; UX rules apply to their overrides only (product-audit/site-shape.md).

19. Revised: docs content belongs to docs-quality, the rendered docs page belongs to UX. Revision 1 gave docs pages wholly to docs-quality, but rules/docs-quality.md:184 says page-level accessibility is governed nowhere (product-audit/config-inventory.md smell 10, contradiction 7).

20. The frame's 'docs-quality covers docs' overstates it: alt text, contrast, keyboard order, table semantics, sidebar and search widget are outside docs-quality by its own statement, so the UX set takes them (rules/docs-quality.md:184, product-audit/config-inventory.md smell 10).

21. The css-theming gap in the fleet is drift, not mechanics: 6 consumers on 5 theme specifiers, catalog on ^0.5.0 while the theme is 0.7.0; the version-currency rule belongs to css-theming, not ux-quality (product-audit/site-shape.md smell 4, contradiction 4).

22. One domain, several sites, divergent chrome: three CommandBar/SiteHeader/SiteFooter copies and 8 of 17 nav entries planned: true make WCAG 3.2.3, 3.2.4 and 3.2.6 a live fleet question (product-audit/site-shape.md smells 5 and 10, ux-topic-map/accessibility.md row 5).
23. Agent workers cannot run real assistive technology; announcement tests use a named virtual screen reader or label the claim UNVERIFIED (ux-topic-map/accessibility.md row 34, map row M012).
